title: Nethercore ZX Tool Preview
subtitle: Rollback-first runtime and toolchain review packet
audience: Fighting game developers evaluating the platform/tooling, not prototype game content.
description: Nethercore ZX is a rollback-first fantasy console/runtime for deterministic 2D and 3D games. The review ask is whether the runtime, toolchain, examples, and constraints look credible for fighting game development.
nonGoals: This is not a finished fighting game.
Prototype fighting-game content is not the showcase.
Online product UX, matchmaking, lobbies, and ranked systems are not the current review target.
reviewGoals: Does the init/update/render model make sense for rollback-heavy games?
Are the determinism rules clear enough for serious fighting game prototyping?
Do the build, ROM packaging, asset loading, debug, replay, and capture tools look useful?
What is missing before this would feel trustworthy for a fighting game project?

examples.title: Debug Demo
examples.why: Debug inspector and runtime variable registration.

examples.title: EPU Showcase
examples.why: Procedural environment/background tooling and inspector workflow.

examples.title: GLB Inline
examples.why: Raw GLB references converted at pack time.

examples.title: Paddle
examples.why: Small complete game loop and rollback-safe multiplayer example. Not a content quality showcase.

feedbackQuestions: Where would you bounce off first as a fighting game developer?
Does the deterministic WASM model feel practical, restrictive, or both?
Is automatic memory snapshotting a compelling rollback workflow?
What debugging, training, replay, or capture tooling would be mandatory before you trusted this?
What parts feel like warning signs?
Which example or doc clarified the tool best?
Which example or doc should be removed from the review path?
If you were evaluating this for a prototype, what would you ask to see next?
